correctness.rationale: With OR-sponsorship, player-specific linear cost and common 0<q<1/3, the three triangle sponsors can each delete, add the isolated link, switch, or redundantly sponsor existing edges; their exact Katz gains reduce to ell(q)<=a<=U(q). The isolate has a strictly convex/supermodular centrality benefit in the number of links to the triangle, so no deviation is profitable iff b>=V(q)=q/(1-3q). Symbolic rational sign checks establish ell<U<V for all 0<q<1/3; exact independent rational-resolvent computations enumerated every unilateral strategy at q=1/4. A triangle graph in any equilibrium cannot contain duplicate sponsors, and deleting an owner edge gives some triangle sponsor cost<=U; the isolate requires cost>=V. A cyclic three-sponsor profile attains V/U, establishing the sharp minimum ratio, approached strictly. The only non-core-periphery graph with <=3 vertices is K2 plus an isolate, excluded because the edge owner could profitably attach the isolate. This proves n=4 minimality without conflating finite checks with the universal rational argument.
